papers.abstract_en: As photometric surveys reach unprecedented statistical precision, systematic uncertainties increasingly dominate large-scale structure probes relying on galaxy number density. Defining the final survey footprint is critical, as it excludes regions affected by artefacts or suboptimal observing conditions. For galaxy clustering, spatially varying observational systematics, such as seeing, are a leading source of bias. Template maps of contaminants are used to derive spatially dependent corrections, but extreme values may fall outside the applicability range of mitigation methods, compromising correction reliability. The complexity and accuracy of systematics modelling depend on footprint conservativeness, with aggressive masking enabling simpler, robust mitigation. We present a unified approach to define the DES Y6 JOINT footprint, integrating observational systematics templates and artefact indicators that degrade mitigation performance. This removes extreme values from an initial SEED footprint, leading to the final JOINT footprint. By evaluating the DES Y6 lens sample MagLim++ on this footprint, we enhance the Iterative Systematics Decontamination (ISD) method, detecting non-linear systematic contamination and improving correction accuracy. While the mask's impact on clustering is less significant than systematics decontamination, it remains non-negligible, comparable to statistical uncertainties in certain w(theta) scales and redshift bins. Supporting coherent analyses of galaxy clustering and cosmic shear, the final footprint spans 4,031.04 deg2, setting the basis for DES Y6 1x2pt, 2x2pt, and 3x2pt analyses. This work highlights how targeted masking strategies optimise the balance between statistical power and systematic control in Stage-III and -IV surveys.

papers.title_en: Disorder-Induced Griffiths like Phase and Charge Localization in Sr2FeRuO6
papers.abstract_en: A comprehensive understanding of complex transition-metal oxides is key to designing next-generation spintronic materials with tailored magnetic and transport functionalities. We investigate the interplay among structural disorder, frustrated magnetism, and localized charge transport in the 3d-4d hybrid double perovskite Sr2FeRuO6. The compound adopts a monoclinic structure with significant B-site antisite disorder that drives its unconventional behavior. Magnetic measurements uncover a robust Griffiths phase extending well above the ordering temperature, evidencing stable short-range ferromagnetic clusters within a disordered matrix. Electrical transport remains strongly localized, transitioning from small-polaron hopping at high temperatures to variable-range hopping at intermediate temperatures. These results position Sr2FeRuO6 as a representative 3d-4d hybrid system in which quenched disorder stabilizes spin inhomogeneity, while polaronic and hopping transport are also observed.

papers.title_en: Identifying heating processes in simulations with an entropy-based scheme: A single jet episode in a galaxy cluster
papers.abstract_en: Understanding heating processes in galaxy clusters is essential for predicting the regulation of radiative cooling and star formation, and for clarifying the mechanisms underlying active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback in cool-core clusters. We investigate the processes through which AGN jets deposit heat into the intracluster medium (ICM) by tracking passive entropy scalars in magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) simulations. This enables us to systematically disentangle the contributions from different heating channels. We successfully validate this method with several idealized tests, including turbulent heating, heating by anisotropic Braginskii viscosity, dissipative and adiabatic heating by shocks using in-situ shock-detection methods, and cosmic ray (CR) heating through the excitations and damping of Alfvén waves. Using this methodology, we simulate single-epoch outbursts of high-power jets with varying densities in a cluster environment. Light jets produce wider bubbles, displacing a larger fraction of the gas in the cluster's core, whereas comparatively denser jets propagate more efficiently to larger distances without significantly disturbing the central region. During early evolution, shock heating of the ICM prevails irrespective of jet density. At later times, light jets primarily heat the ICM through turbulently induced heating (which includes dissipation of vortices emerging from a turbulent cascade and mixing gas of different temperatures) and compressible dissipation of sound waves and very weak shocks, while denser jets continue to dissipate most of their energy via shocks. Particularly, turbulently induced heating by solenoidal-shear motions prevails inside the cocoon, whereas shocks and acoustic compressions dominate outside. In light jets, the forward shock weakens rapidly, whereas dense jets can sustain strong bow shocks to large distances.

papers.title_en: Evolving dark energy and a younger Universe from cosmic inhomogeneity
papers.abstract_en: Joint analyses of baryon acoustic oscillations, type Ia supernovae and the cosmic microwave background show a preference for an evolving dark-energy equation of state, and recent studies suggest that cosmic inhomogeneities can produce an apparent evolution of dark energy within general relativity. Here we examine this effect within a framework in which the possibility that matter can be unevenly distributed enters the expansion dynamics directly. The framework yields redshift-dependent effective values of the Hubble constant and of the dark-energy density parameter without introducing a new free parameter. Using CMB-inferred parameters to fix the homogeneous limit, we find that the dark-energy density parameter increases by about eight percent toward the present, from 0.679 to 0.735, while the inferred Hubble constant shifts from the Planck value toward the range obtained from local measurements. Both trends are broadly consistent with published estimates from supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, X-ray clusters and gravitational waves, although a joint analysis of the underlying data is left for future work. Integrating the resulting expansion history gives a present-day cosmic age of 13.521 Gyr, compared with 13.827 Gyr for the homogeneous model; we interpret the difference of 0.306 Gyr as a global time dilation between the two descriptions. The framework also yields the homogeneous-limit dark-energy density parameter, two thirds, from the formation of volume alone. The predicted redshift dependences can be tested against forthcoming measurements of cosmic distances and expansion rates.

papers.title_en: Unconventional quantum spin mixing of two spin-1 atoms beyond the single-mode approximation
papers.abstract_en: The single-mode approximation (SMA) has been widely employed in ultracold spinor gases, where all spin components share the same spatial mode. By adopting generalized Van Vleck (GVV) perturbation theory, we achieve a relative error of $10^{-6}$ in the ground-state energy with a reduced effective Hilbert space dimension of $\sim 10^3$ for two spin-1 bosons confined in a one-dimensional hard-wall trap. With the accurate GVV method, we explore the validity of the SMA across ground-state properties and quench spin dynamics for two $^{7}\text{Li}$, $^{87}\text{Rb}$, or $^{23}\text{Na}$ atoms. Numerical results show that the quadratic Zeeman energy $q$ provides a powerful control knob: by increasing $|q|$, the fidelity between the spin components in the ground state gradually decreases, leading eventually to the breakdown of the SMA (due to the competition between the kinetic energy and the quadratic Zeeman energy). Quench spin dynamics with abruptly increased $q$ further reveals multiple resonances, where the SMA-predicted micromotion and beyond-SMA macromotion appear simultaneously. These results point to a direction to investigate the quantum spin-mixing dynamics beyond the SMA, particularly in recent experiments of strongly interacting spin-1 atomic gases.

papers.title_en: Cosmo-PINN: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Cosmological Reconstruction
papers.abstract_en: We introduce Cosmo-PINN, a Physics-Informed Neural Network for reconstruction of the cosmological theory. In this work we demonstrate the application of the Cosmo-PINN in the reconstruction of the dark energy equation of state parameter $w_{DE}\left( z\right) $ directly from late-time cosmological observations. This framework overcomes the main limitation shared by Gaussian Process and Artificial Neural Network reconstruction approaches, where the recovered solution is driven by the data and it is not necessarily true that it is physically consistent, by embedding the cosmological constraints directly into the loss function as constraints, ensuring that the reconstructed quantities satisfy the physical laws at every point during the training. For the training of the network, we employed background data, and specifically the Baryon Acoustic Oscillation from DESI DR2, the Cosmic Chronometers and three different Supernova compilations, while we simultaneously introduce the cosmological parameters $% H_{0},~Ω_{m0}$ and $r_{\mathrm{drag}}$ as trained parameters. The reconstruction shows that the trained $w_{DE}\left( z\right) $ crosses the phantom divide around $z=0.5$ in agreement with the value obtained by the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder model. In the quintessence scenario, the dark energy equation of state parameter is forced to the $Λ$CDM limit in the past, that is $w_{DE}\left( z\right) \rightarrow -1 $. Finally, we demonstrate the significance of imposing the physical constraints within the loss function by comparing the Cosmo-PINN reconstruction against a purely data-driven neural network with the same architecture.

papers.title_en: The stellar-to-halo mass relation of central galaxies across three orders of halo mass
papers.abstract_en: The stellar content of galaxies is tightly connected to the mass and growth of their host dark matter halos. Observational constraints on this relation remain limited, particularly for low-mass groups, leaving uncertainties in how galaxies assemble their stars across halo mass scales. Accurately measuring the brightest central galaxy (BCG) stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR) over a wide mass range is therefore crucial for understanding galaxy formation and the role of feedback processes. Here we present the SHMR spanning $M_{\rm halo} \sim 10^{12}$-$10^{15}\,M_\odot$, using halo masses derived from eROSITA eRASS1 X-ray data and BCG stellar masses based on SDSS photometry. By stacking X-ray spectra of optically selected groups, we recover robust average halo gas temperatures for each bin, which are then converted to halo masses via the $M$-$T_X$ relation. We find that the SHMR peaks near $M_{\rm halo} \sim 10^{12}\,M_\odot$, with a declining stellar fraction at higher masses. This trend reflects a combination of processes that reduce the efficiency of stellar mass growth in massive halos, such as AGN feedback, reduced cooling efficiency, and the increasing dominance of ex-situ assembly, while halos continue to grow through mergers and accretion. Our measurements are consistent over the full mass range with previous observational studies, including weak lensing, X-ray analyses of individual clusters, and kinematical and dynamical methods. Comparisons with hydrodynamical simulations show good agreement at low masses but reveal significant discrepancies in the normalization at cluster scales, highlighting the sensitivity of BCG stellar growth to feedback prescriptions and halo assembly history. These results provide the first X-ray-based observational SHMR covering three orders of magnitude in halo mass, establish a robust benchmark for testing galaxy formation models.

papers.title_en: Flares and flux ropes: an entangled story
papers.abstract_en: Solar flares serve as standard candles for all magnetic-reconnection-based energy releases, and their consequences into the heliosphere can be modeled from first principles. This review presents the latest developments in modeling solar flares and their associated flux rope expulsions with state-of-the-art multidimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) descriptions. Observationally established ingredients beyond a single-fluid, thermal plasma evolution have been incorporated to varying degrees, and we highlight self-consistent efforts realized in "standard flare" setups.

papers.title_en: Delayed Radio Flares in Neutrino-associated Blazars: The Case of TXS 0506+056
papers.abstract_en: Radio flares have been postulated to be associated with the production of astrophysical neutrinos. For example, TXS 0506+056 exhibits a 2-3 yr delay between the 2017 IceCube-170922A/gamma-ray flare and a GHz radio maximum. We quantitatively test if the delayed radio flare originates from the same compact region where neutrinos and gamma-rays are produced as it expands downstream and synchrotron self-absorption (SSA) is reduced. Starting from the 2017 flare blob parameters, we model the expanding production region and its evolving radio emission with LeHaMoC in a fully time-dependent framework, and compare our 1.2-22 GHz light curves to RATAN-600 data. We study different scenarios with increasing levels of sophistication, including continuous injection and energy re-dissipation on pc scales. While a simple expanding blob scenario fails to reproduce the radio data, a downstream dissipation episode of particles in the optically thin regime, followed by jet deceleration, successfully describes the radio evolution. The radio flare is powered by leptonic synchrotron emission and is largely insensitive to the proton population relevant for neutrino production, implying that the delayed radio flare mainly probes downstream dissipation and beaming in certain jet configurations instead of being a direct radiative counterpart of the compact neutrino-production zone.

papers.title_en: Time-reversed stochastic inflation in the quantum well
papers.abstract_en: Time-reversed stochastic inflation solves the stochastic evolution of the inflationary universe backward in time, by counting the number of e-folds from the end of quantum diffusion towards some initial state. The point of view of observers attached to the end-of-inflation hypersurface is thus enforced. In this work, we exactly solve time-reversed stochastic inflation in a flat and bounded potential, the so-called quantum well. At given lifetime, the field behaviour is found to be either indistinguishable from the one obtained in a semi-infinite flat potential, or, subject to enhanced stochasticity where any memory of the initial state is erased. The derived distribution of curvature perturbations reduces to the semi-infinite result for small fluctuations while it develops exponential tails for the large ones. Such tails arise for both positive and negative values, and decay twice as fast as the one obtained in the standard forward stochastic inflation. These differences may have important consequences for tail-sensitive phenomena, such as primordial black hole formation.

papers.title_en: Dicke model of open-shell atoms with tensor polarizability
papers.abstract_en: We study the extended Dicke model obtained from the scalar--vector--tensor polarizability of open-shell atoms coupled to a shared cavity mode. For a single electric-dipole channel, rotational symmetry fixes the tensor to vector ratio; we use $^{168}\mathrm{Er}$ with $J=6$ as a product-state example. A circular pump produces a chiral Raman vertex whose tensor-dependent matrix elements select the occupied Zeeman sector. The resulting first-order transition occurs before the empty-cavity branch loses local stability, and the ordered state is read out through $\langle\hat J_z\rangle$. A linear pump instead produces an empty-cavity $\pm x$ cat and a continuous transition into an even-$m$ cat-like state with order parameter $\langle\hat J_z^2\rangle$. With cavity loss alone, the circular trajectory emits a photon burst and approaches a Raman-dark Zeeman pole rather than a finite-field condensate. In the linear geometry, cavity-bright modes are damped toward the cat-like branch while a dark spin mode remains undamped. These are phenomena of that model; the vector-only controls show that they depend on the channel-fixed tensor coupling.

papers.title_en: Conformal Anomalies and Generalised Energy Conservation in De Sitter Spacetime
papers.abstract_en: We show that for bulk discrete series fields whose dual operators have integer conformal dimensions, the Generalised Energy Conservation (GEC) condition for de Sitter (dS) scattering amplitudes defined in even-dimensional extended Poincaré spacetime corresponds precisely to the absence of boundary conformal anomalies, including beta-function contributions, at the level of tree-level contact interactions. In contrast, holographic consistency in AdS/CFT enforces only the locality of the conformal anomaly. We find novel, unique four-point interactions involving three identical conformally coupled scalars and one discrete series scalar by performing both GEC and holographic bootstraps. This demonstrates that the solutions to GEC form a measure-zero subset of the holographically consistent solutions. Our holographic analysis agrees precisely with the expected renormalisation conditions for conformal field theory correlators. In addition, the constraint for a particular four-point configuration may be relevant for testing holographic consistency of scale-separated non-supersymmetric AdS$_4$ vacua.

papers.title_en: $S$-duality, boundary states, and higher-form symmetries on ALE spaces
papers.abstract_en: We study Abelian $S$-duality of Maxwell theory on $A$-type asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) spaces. Unlike on closed four-manifolds, the Maxwell path integral on an ALE space is not naturally a scalar partition function. Rather, it decomposes into theta-function blocks labeled by flat $U(1)$ holonomy sectors on the asymptotic lens-space boundary. We interpret these blocks as components of the Hilbert-space boundary state prepared by the ALE path integral. With this interpretation, the apparent failure of ordinary modularity is replaced by vector-valued modular covariance under the action of the modular group. We test this picture explicitly for Eguchi-Hanson space by gluing it to its orientation reversal. The resulting closed four-manifold is diffeomorphic to $S^2\times S^2$, and the natural pairing of the two ALE boundary states reproduces the standard Maxwell partition function on $S^2\times S^2$. We then refine the construction by turning on electric and magnetic $1$-form symmetry backgrounds. In their presence, the ALE theta blocks are not ordinary functions, but sections of a line bundle over the Cartan torus associated with the $A_{N-1}$ root lattice, reflecting the mixed electric-magnetic $1$-form anomaly. We also discuss gauging discrete $\mathbb Z_k$ subgroups of the $1$-form symmetries and show that the vector-valued boundary-state structure remains the natural covariant framework after gauging. In this sense, ALE spaces behave as chiral building blocks for four-dimensional Maxwell theory: individual ALE blocks carry sector-resolved boundary data, while gluing pairs these sectors to produce an ordinary closed-manifold partition function, much like the pairing of left- and right-moving conformal blocks in two-dimensional CFT.

papers.title_en: Testing Charged Black Holes Embedded in Anisotropic Matter and Surrounded by Plasma through Gravitational Lensing: Bounds from the Sloan Lens ACS Survey
papers.abstract_en: We investigate weak gravitational lensing by a charged black hole surrounded by anisotropic matter, described by the two-component Kiselev metric, and immersed in a homogeneous plasma. We first examine the black hole geometry and horizon structure and then derive the weak-deflection angle from the Hamiltonian description of light propagation in plasma, using an expansion with a fixed turning point that we verify against direct numerical integration. Using the gravitational lens equation, we obtain the Einstein-ring angle, the image positions, the total magnification and the fractional magnifications of the primary and secondary images. We then confront the model with the Einstein radii of two galaxy-scale lenses of the Sloan Lens ACS Survey, J0008$-$0004 and J0029$-$0055. Because the Einstein angle cannot be smaller than the reduced deficit deflection, the observed radii give the mass-independent bounds $K<6.5\times10^{-6}$ and $K<4.2\times10^{-6}$, respectively. The charge correction to the Einstein radius is suppressed by $r_s/R_E\approx 5\times10^{-6}$ and is unobservable, while the plasma parameter at the optical wavelengths of the SLACS imaging is of order $10^{-22}$ and cannot be constrained. Our results show that galaxy-scale strong lensing data place stringent limits on anisotropic matter surrounding the lens, whereas plasma effects can be probed only at low radio frequencies.

papers.title_en: Stationary Resistive MHD Solutions Near an Isolated Three-Dimensional Magnetic Null
papers.abstract_en: Magnetic null points define the magnetic field topology in stellar coronae, planetary magnetospheres, and astrospheres, and are commonly associated with magnetic reconnection. We investigate the local structure of stationary three-dimensional (3D) resistive, incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flows in the vicinity of an isolated magnetic null and an isolated velocity stagnation point, assuming that the two nulls are colocated. The governing MHD equations are solved self-consistently using a first-order local expansion of the magnetic and velocity fields about the null. For any given magnetic-null configuration, the equations admit a two-parameter family of stationary solutions, comprising multiple solution branches with distinct velocity topologies. Along these families, the velocity-null polarity can change at bifurcation points where the flow becomes effectively 2.5D. A single magnetic null can therefore support positive-radial, negative-radial, and spiral stagnation flows, with qualitatively different inflow, outflow, and rotational properties. The associated pressure and resistivity distributions are likewise determined self-consistently and vary across the solution family, demonstrating that they are coupled to the flow topology rather than prescribed independently. The generic solutions do not require the velocity and magnetic separatrices to coincide, allowing plasma to cross the magnetic fan separatrix and providing a local reconnective flow. These results demonstrate that, in the presence of nonuniform resistivity, the magnetic topology alone does not uniquely determine the associated stationary flow, pressure, or resistivity structure around a 3D magnetic null, revealing the nonlinear feedback between all macroscopic variables and resistivity. The constant-resistivity field-aligned and spiral field-crossing solutions identified previously are recovered as special cases.

papers.title_en: Multi-Instantons and Exact-WKB Stokes Jumps in Multi-Well Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract_en: We study the relation between the exact-WKB Delabaere--Dillinger--Pham Stokes jumps and the multi-instanton expansion of a one-dimensional potential with $N$ equal-depth minima. For a single barrier this relation is the Bogomolny--Zinn-Justin cancellation between the instanton--anti-instanton ambiguity and the Borel ambiguity of perturbation theory, and we extend it to every consecutive barrier interval and to the integration contours themselves. In the dilute large-$T$ regime at fixed nonperturbative grade, we derive the quasi-zero mode integral over the instanton separations from the Euclidean path integral and reduce it to Gamma and Hankel periods. With the local Weber level function of each well and one normalization per well fixed by the local Weber connection matrix, these periods reproduce the two lateral connected exact-WKB coefficients. The two lateral contours of each instanton--anti-instanton separation differ by exactly one Hankel cycle, and this linear Picard--Lefschetz relation reproduces the Stokes jump of the connected coefficient. A numerical solution of the Schrödinger equation for a symmetric triple well confirms the resulting two-barrier level splitting. At higher fixed grade, the map from ordered event sequences to normalized scalar coefficient products is not one-to-one. At leading dilute order the scalar weight of a closed event sequence depends only on the numbers of barrier crossings, $\mathcal I\bar{\mathcal I}$ pairs, and $\mathcal I\mathcal I$/$\bar{\mathcal I}\bar{\mathcal I}$ pairs. We construct two inequivalent grade-six triple-well event sequences with the same product of local Weber amplitudes, which embed in every potential with $N\ge3$ wells. Our results hold within the regular dilute, one-loop, local Weber approximation.

papers.title_en: Testing Departures from the $Λ$CDM model in f(T) Gravity with DESI DR2
papers.abstract_en: Recent analyses combining DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements with other cosmological observations have reported indications of departures from the $Λ$CDM model within dynamical dark energy scenarios. We investigate whether such deviations are reproduced consistently in $f(T)$ gravity and whether they persist when different cosmological observations are combined. Using the DESI DR2 BAO measurements, Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), and Pantheon+ Type Ia Supernovae (SNe Ia) sample, we constrain three representative $f(T)$ models: the power-law, exponential, and hyperbolic-tangent models. We compare the constraints obtained from different combinations of data, distinguishing changes in marginalized parameter distributions from changes in the relative statistical performance of the models. For the power-law model, the mild deviation from the $Λ$CDM model obtained from BAO+CMB disappears after the SNe Ia data are included. In contrast, the exponential model retains a preference for a nonzero deformation parameter in the full analysis, while the allowed parameter space of the hyperbolic-tangent model changes substantially after the CMB distance priors are included. Importantly, the parameter-level deviation found for the exponential model does not lead to a clear statistical preference over the $Λ$CDM model according to the information criteria, whereas the hyperbolic-tangent model shows a poorer statistical performance for the combined data. Despite these differences in the model constraints, the inferred transition redshift $z_T$ remains relatively stable among the three models and data combinations. Our results show that the departures from the $Λ$CDM model indicated by DESI analyses are not a generic feature of $f(T)$ gravity, but depend strongly on the specific modified gravity parameterization and on the combination of cosmological observations.

papers.title_en: Deep Learning of Phase Transitions for Bilinear-Biquadratic Spin-1 Chains from Correlation Aspects
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the role of different correlation functions in reconstructing the phase diagram of the spin-1 bilinear-biquadratic chain, parametrized by the angle $θ$ between the bilinear and biquadratic couplings, using our previously developed label-free machine-learning pipeline \cite{Ming21, Ming23}, in which an autoencoder compresses iDMRG correlation matrices into latent features and K-means clustering with silhouette analysis groups them into phases. Without any prior labels, the scheme reveals four natural phases, the Haldane, dimerized, critical trimerized, and ferromagnetic phases, and accurately locates the Takhtajan-Babujian ($θ=-π/4$), $SU(3)$-symmetric Uimin-Lai-Sutherland ($θ=π/4$), and Ferro-Dimer ($θ=5π/4$) transition points; a shallow supervised refinement further sharpens the phase boundaries. We find that different correlation functions play fundamentally different roles in phase identification. The $SU(3)$-symmetric correlation alone selects a four-cluster partition that can be associated with the four phases, whereas the spin-spin and dimer-dimer correlations must be combined to recover the complete phase diagram. In contrast, the trimer-trimer correlation behaves as a marginal correlation: it is insufficient for phase identification by itself but improves the precision of the predicted phase boundaries when combined with the other correlations. Furthermore, the latent representations and silhouette values reveal signatures that we relate to the $θ$ dependence of the correlations within each phase and, tentatively, to the underlying renormalization-group structure. These results demonstrate that machine learning can not only identify quantum phases but also uncover the physical information encoded in different correlation functions.

papers.title_en: Quantum Field Theory Of Cosmological Perturbations Induced By Ultralight Dark Matter
papers.abstract_en: The growth of primordial perturbations during the matter-dominated era is primarily driven by dark matter. Ultralight scalar fields (ULDM) are a promising candidate for this role, conventionally modeled as operating in a classical, high-occupation regime. In this work, we develop a first-principles field-theoretic framework to investigate the impact of ULDM on linear cosmological perturbations during matter domination, explicitly retaining its quantum nature. Deriving a closed equation for the graviton field dynamics, we compute and regularize its source terms for a generic Gaussian initial state of the ULDM field within the adiabatic (WKB) approximation, employing the middle-point working assumption for non-local terms. After gauge-fixing we find that, contrary to previous claims, the classical condensate of ULDM has no influence on gravitational wave propagation. However, the time-dependent graviton effective mass induced by quantum pressure of the squeezed state can drive parametric resonance in specific primordial gravitational wave modes. We demonstrate this growth is negligible for non-relativistic ULDM at matter-radiation equality under the assumption of a power-law squeezing spectrum for masses in the range $m \sim 10^{-21}{-}10^{-24}$ eV.

papers.title_en: Cluster algebra and quasimap quantum cohomology
papers.abstract_en: We apply the abelianization technique to obtain an explicit ring presentation for the quasimap quantum cohomology of GIT quotients. As an application, for quiver varieties associated with oriented-acyclic quivers, we establish a cluster algebra structure on their equivariant quasimap quantum cohomology rings.

papers.title_en: Data augmentation by an electro-vibratory feedback improves signal interpretation by neural networks
papers.abstract_en: Data-driven machine learning algorithms represent an alternative to numerical or analytical modeling of vibrating objects for the purpose of extracting their material or geometric properties. Their performance is conditioned by the quality of the training dataset, which should contain all possible production configurations of the object and measurement conditions. In this work, we propose a data-augmentation method based on manipulations of the vibration properties rather than numerical signal post-processing. Instead of modifying the sample’s material or geometry, we connect an additional sensor and actuator to the sample and use low-latency electronics to control the feedback signal. This delivers an electromechanical system with tunable oscillation properties. This signal diversification method is demonstrated on the classification of correct and incorrect adhesion of two aluminum plates. The labeling accuracy of 67% on nine unknown test objects, when trained on a single unchangeable training object, increases to 83% when the variety of the training vibration signals is augmented by varying the parameters of the electrovibratory feedback. This provides advantages for industrial quality control, where a large number of reference training samples are not available.

papers.title_en: u-d Quark Matter in the Enhanced pQCD Model and u-d Quark Stars in Gravity’s Rainbow
The Search for Mev-scale Neutrinos in Temporal Coincidence With o4 Gravitational Wave Events Using the Sno+ Experiment
papers.abstract_en: This dissertation presents a search for low-energy neutrinos in temporal coincidence with gravitational wave events reported by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration during the fourth observing run (O4), using 499.0 days of data collected during the liquid scintillator phase of the SNO+ experiment. The search uses inverse beta decay (IBD), which is primarily sensitive to electron antineutrinos, and neutrino-proton elastic scattering, a complementary neutral current channel providing sensitivity to all neutrino flavors. Candidate events were identified using optimized reconstruction and event-selection criteria developed with Monte Carlo simulations and validated with background-only data. The IBD background rate was measured directly from data, naturally incorporating reactor antineutrinos, geoneutrinos, radioactive backgrounds, cosmogenic backgrounds, and accidental coincidences present during detector operation. A model-independent framework was developed using flat spectrum neutrino Monte Carlo samples, allowing the detector response to be evaluated as a function of neutrino energy and applied to different theoretical emission models. As part of this work, improvements were made to the SNO+ Monte Carlo simulation, including modifications to the IBD generator to produce a true flat neutrino spectrum and corrections to the implementation of the neutrino-proton elastic scattering cross section. Detector characterization studies, including measurements of the deployed scintillator light yield and investigations of detector timing and electronics performance, were also performed to validate the detector response used throughout the analysis. The final gravitational wave-coincident dataset contained 143 candidates overlapping stable SNO+ data-taking periods. After excluding candidates classified as terrestrial or unknown by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration, the final astrophysical sample used for compact binary merger fluence limits contained 126 gravitational wave candidates. No statistically significant neutrino excess was observed in either the IBD or neutrino-proton elastic scattering channels. The IBD search observed no coincident candidates in the final astrophysical gravitational wave sample, consistent with an expected background of 1.25 ± 0.09 events. The corresponding Feldman-Cousins 90% confidence level upper limit is N90stack = 1.47 signal events. Stacked average (per gravitational wave) upper limits on the electron antineutrino fluence were derived for both monoenergetic neutrino emission and model-dependent spectra, including thermal neutrino and core-collapse supernova-inspired models used as detector sensitivity benchmarks. The neutrino-proton elastic scattering search represents the first application of this all-flavor channel to a gravitational wave-coincident neutrino search. Using an optimized ±50 s coincidence window, 108424 candidate events were observed, consistent with the expected background of 108345 ± 786 events estimated from local sidebands. The observed 0.24σ fluctuation is consistent with the background-only hypothesis. For the final astrophysical gravitational wave sample, the Feldman-Cousins method gives a 90% confidence level upper limit of N90stack = 1479.6 signal events. These results are used to derive the first all-flavor neutrino-proton elastic scattering fluence limits associated with compact binary merger candidates. The resulting SNO+ IBD fluence limits improve upon previous liquid scintillator gravitational wave-neutrino searches by approximately an order of magnitude in the few-MeV energy region, primarily due to the larger fiducial target mass, increased gravitational wave sample size, and low background rate achieved in SNO+. The neutrino-proton elastic scattering results establish the first all-flavor MeV neutrino search through this interaction channel in coincidence with gravitational wave events. Together, these analyses extend previous multi-messenger searches performed by Borexino, KamLAND, and Super-Kamiokande and demonstrate the capability of SNO+ to search for weak neutrino signals associated with astrophysical transients.

papers.title_en: ESC Enables Protection of an Accelerator Superconducting Magnet With $>$5 kA/mm$^{2}$ Copper Current Density
papers.abstract_en: A new quench-protection technique, energy shift with coupling (ESC), has recently been proposed and shows significant promise for the protection of high-field magnets. The ESC system includes normal-conducting coils that are strongly magnetically coupled to, but galvanically insulated from, the magnet coils. When activated, the system rapidly transfers energy from the magnet to the ESC coils, substantially reducing ohmic losses at the magnet hot spot and promoting the transition of the superconducting coils to the normal state through transient losses. During the subsequent magnet-current discharge, part of the stored magnetic energy is transferred to the ESC coils. ESC was recently demonstrated successfully at CERN on a 400 mm long flat racetrack magnet structure without an aperture. In this work, we present the application of the ESC method to a subscale common-coil magnet known as the subscale stress-managed common-coil series (subSMCC2), designed and manufactured by the Magnet Development Laboratory at the Paul Scherrer Institute. The subSMCC2 is a 300 mm long magnet comprising four stress-managed Nb₃Sn common coils and is designed to reach bore and peak coil fields of approximately 5.3 T and 6.4 T, respectively, at a short-sample current of 9.5 kA. Protecting this magnet following a quench, without the use of energy extraction, is particularly challenging because of its very high stabilizer current density, exceeding 5 kA/mm². The proposed ESC-based protection scheme employs two common-coil-type ESC coils made from rectangular copper conductors and located on the outer sides of the magnet coils. Tests performed at the CERN magnet test facility successfully demonstrated the performance of the ESC system under a variety of operating conditions. These results show that ESC is an effective, high-performance quench-protection technology capable of protecting magnets operating at very high current densities.

papers.title_en: Quantum Key Distribution Network Simulator With Hyperparameter Tuning for Realistic Performance Analysis
papers.abstract_en: Realistic simulation of quantum key distribution (QKD) networks requires a combination of precise models of quantum channels and network functions. Unfortunately, existing QKD network simulators lack either rigorous quantum physics modeling or network key-management and routing protocols, which limit their practical applicability. To address this limitation, we propose a QKD network simulator with hyperparameter tuning (QKDSim-HT), a NetSquid-based simulator specialized for polarization-based discrete-variable QKD networks. Specifically, QKDSim-HT models properties in quantum physics (photon loss, polarization-dependent depolarization, detector inefficiencies, dark counts, and dead times) as well as advanced functionalities in networking algorithms (multi-hop key relay and adaptive routing). Extensive simulations over diverse topologies reveal that the networking performance varied with respect to the fundamental properties of quantum physics, such as depolarization, fiber length, and channel attenuation. As a representative use case of QKDSim-HT, simulation results from QKDSim-HT over simple examples clearly manifest that a design of QKD networks highly affects performance of the networks. Accordingly, QKDSim-HT can serve as a practical platform for performance evaluation and optimization of quantum secured network.

papers.title_en: Suppression of two-stream and Weibel instabilities in ultra-relativistic electron–positron plasma
papers.abstract_en: We present a unified theoretical framework for analyzing both electrostatic two-stream and electromagnetic Weibel instabilities in counterstreaming electron-positron pair plasmas. Through systematic derivation of dispersion relations in non-relativistic and relativistic regimes, we demonstrate how the symmetric mass ratio fundamentally alters instability characteristics compared to electron-ion systems. The two-stream instability, driven by longitudinal electrostatic perturbations parallel to beam motion, exhibits enhanced growth rates in pair plasmas due to equal contributions from both species, with relativistic suppression scaling as γ0−3 for both electrons and positrons. The Weibel instability, arising from transverse electromagnetic modes perpendicular to streaming directions, lacks the heavy-ion stabilization present in electron-ion plasmas, producing broader unstable spectral ranges and modified saturation levels. We derive explicit conditions determining the relative dominance of each mechanism across parameter space defined by drift velocity, wavenumber orientation, and relativistic Lorentz factor. Our analysis shows that longitudinal two-stream modes dominate at small perpendicular wavenumbers and moderate drift velocities, while transverse Weibel modes become prevalent at high perpendicular wavenumbers and large velocity spreads or temperature anisotropies. These findings have direct implications for understanding magnetic field generation, particle acceleration, and energy dissipation in astrophysical pair plasmas including pulsar wind nebulae, gamma-ray burst internal shocks, and active galactic nuclei jets where counterstreaming pair populations naturally arise.

papers.title_en: Developing and validating models of open quantum systems in solid-state nanostructures
papers.abstract_en: Realistic quantum devices are open systems, and their behaviour depends not only on the subsystem of interest but also on how the environment is modelled and how the relevant observables are extracted. This thesis studies that problem in three settings. First, we study cavity-assisted qubit readout beyond the dispersive regime. We show that once coherent excitation exchange and dissipation become relevant, a microscopic treatment is needed to describe the readout quantitatively, and the optimal readout is set by a trade-off between signal accumulation and the distinguishability of the readout states. Second, we compare fermionic and spin baths in non-interacting transport models and show that spin baths reproduce fermionic reduced dynamics only in the large-bath weak-coupling limit, while clear deviations appear for smaller baths and near half-filling. Third, we study charge transport in molecular junctions using Automated Compression of Environments (ACE). There, the main difficulty is not the time evolution itself, but the extraction of the transport current, since this observable depends on system-environment correlations and is therefore not contained in the reduced system density matrix alone. We show that a probe-mode construction provides a viable route to reformulate the current as a system observable. This thesis advances our understanding of what is required for accurate modelling of open quantum dynamics across a range of solid-state settings, from cavity-assisted qubit readout to charge transport in molecular junctions.

papers.title_en: Using Printed Circuit Boards and MOSFET Switch Arrays Toward the Reliable Manufacture of Superconducting Rectifiers
papers.abstract_en: Using superconducting rectifiers to energize high-temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets is a promising approach to accelerate the uptake of HTS magnet technology. In this work, we start to address two limitations of the HTS superconducting rectifier concepts published to date; their low magnet charging voltages, and the variable properties of their HTS-based switches. Our approach is to test a centre-tapped full-wave transformer–rectifier utilizing HTS secondary windings and switch-arrays of Si <sc xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mosfet</small>s mounted on a printed-circuit board (PCB). This approach has the advantage of greatly facilitating reproducible and reliable manufacture. The rectifier demonstrated magnet charging voltages exceeding a cycle-averaged 80 mV at 100 A and with typically more than 30% of the power supplied to the primary coils delivered to the magnet. We found it to be resilient to our preliminary thermal-cycling testing, with no degradation in performance observed over eight liquid-nitrogen to ambient (77–295 K) thermal cycles. We compare the impact of voltage- and current-controlled modes for the rectifier’s power supply. Our conclusion is that superconducting rectifiers using <sc xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mosfet</small> switch arrays placed on PCBs is a very promising approach for low-current HTS magnet power supplies.

papers.title_en: Compact High Turns Ratio Superconducting Transformer: Comparison Between Cu and REBCO Winding Materials
papers.abstract_en: Compact high turns ratio superconducting transformers are used to transfer power between low-current copper/ semiconductor-based circuits and high-current superconductor-based circuits. This type of transformer is a key component in devices, such as superconducting transformer rectifiers and superconducting current source inverters. Typically the copper winding and the superconducting winding are arranged with a turn ratio above 100:1, respectively, and are situated entirely within a cryogenic environment. The ohmic losses associated with the high count copper winding is problematic for most cryogenic applications and demands attention even when low currents on the order of 1–10 A are used. To address this problem, a transformer has been made using rare-earth barium copper oxide (REBCO) high-temperature superconductor (HTS) coated conductor for both the primary and secondary windings. The coupling coefficient and power consumption of this transformer were measured and compared to an equivalent transformer consisting of a copper primary winding and HTS secondary winding. The HTS primary was found to provide a significant reduction in transformer power consumption and a slight improvement to transformer coupling at frequencies below <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>8 Hz. An increased transformer core loss and winding AC loss began to negate these efficiency improvements above <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>8 Hz. In addition, cowinding the primary and secondary windings provided a higher coupling coefficient and lower power consumption for all winding combinations and frequencies tested. Finally, a short discussion on the implications of these findings respect to superconducting transformer rectifiers contextualizes the findings.

papers.title_en: The Primary Interaction Compton Couple algorithm for sorting GRETINA/GRETA interaction points
Alfvénicity and proximity to parallel-mode marginal stability in the slow solar wind
Mechanical Characteristics of Aluminium-Stabilized Stacked REBCO Tape Cable for the CEPC Detector Magnet
papers.abstract_en: This article investigates the mechanical characteristics and critical current performance of aluminum-stabilized stacked REBCO tape cable (ASTC) for the circular electron-positron collider detector magnet. In-plane bending, torsion, and uniaxial tension tests are carried out, combined by finite element analysis. The correlation between critical current and strain under different loading conditions is systematically analyzed, and key mechanical thresholds are determined. Results show that the minimum allowable in-plane bending diameter is 1200 mm. The critical twist pitch is 327 mm. The critical current degrades to 95% of the initial value when the tensile strain in the REBCO tape reaches 0.37%. This study provides essential experimental data and theoretical support for the structural design and engineering application of ASTC in high-field superconducting magnets.

papers.title_en: Designing Josephson Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifiers: EM-Circuit Cosimulation and Experimental Validation
papers.abstract_en: The development of large-scale superconducting quantum computers critically depends on the accurate readout of qubit states. To enable this, cryogenic parametric amplifiers have been proposed and developed, and have since found widespread use in small-signal detection applications. Among various amplifier architectures, Josephson traveling-wave parametric amplifiers (JTWPAs) are widely adopted due to their broad bandwidth, high saturation power, and compatibility with superconducting qubits. In this work, we present a design workflow of JTWPAs based on a cosimulation approach combining electromagnetic (EM) and circuit-level simulation. We apply this method to a uniform JTWPA, comparing our simulation results with experimental data. To mitigate the challenge of constructing lumped-element circuit models usually used in the conventional simulation method, we directly perform full EM analysis of the device to accurately determine its linear response. The extracted S-parameters are then fed into a nonlinear harmonic balance simulator with Josephson junctions modeled as circuit elements. By doing so, the linear and gain properties of the JTWPA are extracted. Different factors that impact device performance including gain compression, phase matching, and fabrication imperfections are further investigated and modeled. A good agreement between simulation and measurements is identified, establishing the effectiveness of our approach in designing quantum parametric amplifiers.

papers.title_en: Mathematics of effective q-plate in polarization optics
papers.abstract_en: The q-plate is a spatially inhomogeneous SU(2) birefringent optical element that has garnered significant interest due to its ability to mediate the spin-orbit interaction of light and facilitate the generation of structured light with singularities. The q-plate features a spatially varying fast axis orientation defined by three parameters: the topological charge q, retardance delta, and the offset angle $alpha_0$. While the parameter alpha_0 can be changed many times by rotation, any change in the charge and/or retardance entails the fabrication of a new plate. This limitation can be overcome through the concept of an effective waveplate, where multiple waveplates, homogeneous or inhomogeneous, are aligned coaxially so that, under specific constraints, the composite system emulates the behavior of a single effective waveplate. This work presents a comprehensive mathematical formalism for realizing an effective waveplate through a cascaded configuration of three q-plates, each chosen as either a quarter-wave q-plate, a half-wave q-plate, or a combination thereof. Some configurations offer tunability of the retardance over the full range from 0 to $2pi$, even though q-plates with fixed retardances of $pi/2$ and pi are used in sequence to form an effective q-plate. This feature enables holonomic polarization walk on the higher-order Poincare sphere. Such a capability holds significant potential for applications involving structured light associated with the higher-order Poincare sphere, particularly in controlled polarization transformations and polarization-topology engineering.

papers.title_en: Bayesian vs Deep learning: Parameter constraints for an anisotropic universe in f(Q) gravity
Quantum at the Edge: Scalable Standalone FPGA Emulator for QAOA-Based Weighted-MaxCut
papers.abstract_en: Quantum computing (QC) emulation is critical for exploring and advancing near-term quantum algorithms, given the ongoing scalability and reliability challenges of quantum hardware. While FPGA-based QC emulators have emerged as efficient alternatives to bridge the gap toward practical quantum computers, most existing solutions depend on high-performance systems, limiting their applicability in embedded and edge environments. In this work, we present a scalable, standalone FPGA-based emulator specialized for resource-constrained systems. Our design targets the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), particularly for the Weighted-MaxCut problem. By leveraging diagonal decomposition and a pipeline-centric hardware architecture, we reduce the computational complexity of QAOA from $\boldsymbol{O(N^{2})}$ to $\boldsymbol{O(N)}$, where $\boldsymbol{N}$ $\boldsymbol{=}$ $\boldsymbol{2^{n}}$ is the state dimension for $\boldsymbol{n}$ qubits. This reformulation and its architectural co-design significantly reduces hardware overhead, enabling larger qubit configurations on edge-level FPGAs. We encapsulate these optimizations into a hardware accelerator called the Quantum MaxCut Accelerator (QMA), which integrates seamlessly into a RISC-V platform, forming a self-contained emulator. Additionally, we introduce QC Emulator eXpress (QEX), a full-stack automation framework that streamlines QMA integration into configurable RISC-V platforms, significantly facilitating rapid and scalable emulator development and deployment. Through extensive prototyping of various QAOA emulators, our experiments confirm that the proposed QMA achieves energy reductions of up to $\textbf{907}\boldsymbol{\times}$ compared to the CPU-only software baseline under the same standalone FPGA/RISC-V setting and reliably supports up to 9 qubits on a mid-tier FPGA. These results demonstrate the energy efficiency and scalability of the proposed system as a self-contained FPGA/RISC-V platform for edge-local QAOA emulation, prototyping, and HW/SW co-design exploration under resource-constrained conditions.

papers.title_en: Theory of double flat-top solitons in coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations
papers.abstract_en: Solitons are fundamental entities in nonlinear wave equations across diverse branches of physics. In systems with competing nonlinearities, a hallmark transition occurs from traditional bell-shaped profiles to flat-top configurations as the norm increases. In this work, we analyze double flat-top solitons in systems of two coupled generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equations. We develop a theoretical and variational framework that provides both physical insight and a computationally efficient description of these eigenstates. In the large-norm regime, and for a broad class of nonlinear potentials supporting flat-top states, we derive explicit analytical expressions for the plateau densities and chemical potentials, together with variational estimates for the interfacial properties characterizing the solutions. These quantities are controlled by algebraic conditions that generalize the Maxwell coexistence condition to coupled wave functions. We show that two-component flat-top solitons may form core–shell configurations, in which a two-component core is surrounded by a shell of the dominant species, as well as no-shell configurations, where both species occupy the same spatial domain. Using the cubic-quintic nonlinearity as a prototypical model, we compare these analytical predictions with direct numerical computations of the stationary states and find excellent agreement in the flat-top regime. The resulting picture admits a natural interpretation in terms of phase coexistence in an effective binary fluid, with kink-like interfaces carrying an excess grand potential that plays the role of a surface tension. This formalism is applicable to diverse physical platforms, including nonlinear optics, multicomponent Bose–Einstein condensates, and Q-ball configurations in relativistic field theories.

papers.title_en: Turning Selection Bias into a New Statistic: Asymmetry and Fringes of Lensed Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract_en: Gravitational waves (GWs) propagating across the Universe can be distorted by intervening lenses, producing characteristic wave-optics signatures. These effects are not incorporated into current matched-filtering searches and can therefore substantially reduce detection efficiency. The underlying mechanism is the signal-consistency test, which measures deviations between the observed and expected signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) distributions. We report a systematic study of the impact of gravitational lensing on signal-consistency tests, using a two-image interference model and representative signal-consistency statistics in both the time and frequency domains. We find that overlapping images produce sharply localized SNR residuals in the time domain, breaking the reflection symmetry of the autocorrelation about the merger time. Although interference fringes produce broadband SNR residuals in the frequency domain, both domains exhibit a minimum for high-mass signals when the fringe structure becomes comparable to the signal bandwidth. This highlights a limitation of current strategies that search for distorted lensed signals only among GW events detected by matched-filtering searches. Exploiting this asymmetry, we develop a statistic that separates selected down-ranked lensed injections from noise-background triggers and paired nonlensed injections, without extending the template bank. Our results establish the first connection between lensing observables and detection, paving the way for the discovery of lensed GWs.

papers.title_en: Dark matter in dense astrophysical objects
Cℓestial harmonics - Applications of Angular Power Spectra to Problems in Astroparticle and Cosmological Physics
Comparing Even Isotope Xenon Form Factors and Their Impact on Dark Matter Direct Detection
A distance functional between cosmological past-lightcones: the characterization of a scale–dependent inhomogeneity field in high–precision cosmology
DUNE High Band-Width Data Processing Pipeline
papers.abstract_en: The collaboration between NVIDIA and Fermilab will create a high-bandwidth data processing pipeline which uses state of the art Artificial Intelligence to analyze data generated by Fermilab’s DUNE. The collaboration will enable data generated by the experiment to be analyzed close to the source, reducing networking, storage, and time requirements for offline data analysis. The collaboration will analyze potential current and future hardware solutions enabling real‐time analysis of data, as well as performance analysis and improvements based on the LArCV2 codebase to support the performance of goals of the experiment and associated equipment.

papers.title_en: Machine Learning Techniques for Particle Tracking and Boosted Higgs-Boson Pair Searches at the LHC
Commutative exact superalgebras and super-modular tensor categories
papers.abstract_en: We extend the theory of commutative exact algebras in braided finite tensor categories (Shimizu-Yadav) to superalgebras, motivated by extensions of vertex operator (super)algebras. For a braided category $\C$ let $\B=\C^{\gr}$ be the category of Z/2-graded objects with the Koszul-signed braiding. It is the underlying category of the supercategory of Creutzig-Kanade-McRae. A supercommutative superalgebra A=A0⊕A1 in $\C$ is the same as a commutative algebra $\bA$ in $\B$, and super-local modules are the local $\bA$-modules. Hence rigidity, pivotality and ribbon statements are instances of the ordinary theorems, with the ribbon condition $θ_{A_0}=\id$, $θ_{A_1}=\varepsilon\,\id$, where ε=±1 is fixed by the statistics of the odd part. For $\C$ non-degenerate and $\bA$ haploid and exact we prove that the category of super-local modules is a braided finite tensor category whose Müger center is sVect. It is the centralizer of a fermion in a non-degenerate category obtained by condensing in $\C\boxtimes(\text{toric code})$. If $\C$ is ribbon and $\bA$ is symmetric Frobenius it is ribbon. We construct examples from graded simple currents, treat the free fermion and the symplectic fermion, and compare with Creutzig-Kanade-McRae and Creutzig-McRae-Shimizu-Yadav.

papers.title_en: Bubble structure: An insight from the nuclear shape, isospin asymmetry, and charge form factor of Yb isotopes
papers.abstract_en: The effects of shape evolution, pairing correlation, and isospin asymmetry on the bubble structure and the symmetry energy of nuclei have been studied systematically for the even-even Yb isotopes within the covariant density functional theory. The shape of nuclei turns out to play its role in the central depletion. The prolate shape nuclei exhibit more pronounced bubble characteristics than the nuclei with oblate configuration, while the pairing correlation reduces the depletion. The depletion fraction in the region of the major shell with the <math><mrow><mn>3</mn><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> orbital decreases with an increase in quadrupole deformation, and occupation probabilities of the <math><mrow><mn>3</mn><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> orbital. Beyond the fully occupied <math><mrow><mn>3</mn><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> energy level, the depletion increases with an increase in the isospin asymmetry parameter. The nuclear deformation and the presence of central depletion are found to impact the nuclear charge form factors and phase shifts, and thus provide direct signatures in electron-nucleus scattering. The charge form-factor analysis, including relativistic spin-orbit and Darwin-Foldy corrections, reveals that the observed diffraction patterns in deformed Yb isotopes arise from a nontrivial interplay among central density depletion, nuclear size, and shape-induced modifications of the monopole charge-density distribution. Scaling the momentum transfer with the rms charge radius demonstrates that the form-factor differences cannot be attributed solely to nuclear size, while residual differences indicate a measurable sensitivity to the underlying interior density profile.

papers.title_en: Isomeric states in odd-<math><mi>A</mi></math> tantalum isotopes with <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>106</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>116</mn></mrow></math>
papers.abstract_en: The structure of high-<math><mi>K</mi></math> isomeric states in the odd-<math><mi>A</mi></math> tantalum <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>73</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> isotopes is investigated systematically within the cranked Nilsson–Strutinsky (CNS) and cranked Nilsson–Strutinsky–Bogoliubov (CNSB) frameworks, spanning neutron numbers <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>106</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>116</mn></mrow></math>. The low-lying one-proton isomers are identified with the <math><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>514</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, <math><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>402</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, and <math><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>411</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> Nilsson orbitals, while the two-quasineutron configurations <math><mrow><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math>, <math><msup><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></math>, and <math><msup><mn>10</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></math> are shown to play a decisive role in driving multiquasiparticle isomer formation across the chain. High-<math><mi>K</mi></math> isomers are predicted in <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ta</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>189</mn></mmultiscripts></math> at low excitation energies, presenting a strong motivation for future experiments. The CNSB calculations predict a transition from stable prolate shapes to triaxiality and shape coexistence in odd-<math><mi>A</mi></math> Ta isotopes near <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>114</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>116</mn></mrow></math>.

papers.title_en: Photon climbing in a Kerr ladder for steady nonclassical light generation
papers.abstract_en: We propose a dissipative ladder-climbing mechanism in which <math><mi>N</mi></math> incoherently pumped qubits autonomously stabilize the cavity field near the target <math><mi>N</mi></math>-photon cavity Fock state <math><msub><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>〉</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></msub></math>. Full Lindblad simulations verify the predicted photon-number climbing and show that Kerr-induced spectral selectivity suppresses off-resonant leakage. We further develop an effective analytical approach that agrees quantitatively with full Lindblad steady-state results in the validated parameter regime and enables extrapolation to larger qubit arrays. The stabilized fields remain strongly sub-Poissonian and retain appreciable Wigner negativity, with radial Wigner-function fringes becoming increasingly pronounced at higher <math><mi>N</mi></math>, suggesting a tunable dissipative route from single-photon generation to large-photon-number Fock-state resources relevant to bosonic quantum information processing and quantum-enhanced metrology.

papers.title_en: Sterile neutrino self-interactions in cosmology: from dark matter to the baryon asymmetry
Room for thermal dark matter: from WIMPs to Sub-GeV scales
Phenomenology of lepton flavor violation and dark matter for scotogenic extensions of the Standard Model
Dark matter and CP-violation in extensions of the Standard Model

papers.title_en: Neutrino Self–Interactions in the Dodelson–Widrow Mechanism
Non-planar contact structures with Calabi-Yau Fillings and topological quantum computation
papers.abstract_en: This paper is a non-planar counterpart of the author's earlier work on planar contact structures and topological quantum computation. There the page is planar and all branch points are paired by disjoint liftable arcs, compatibly with the joint eigenlines of the Ising representation and with Calabi-Yau (CY) Stein fillings, those with vanishing first Chern class. Here the page has genus g and connected binding, presented as a simple degree-three cover of the disk. Every maximal system of disjoint liftable arcs has exactly g members and leaves two branch points unused. The half-twist interchanging the two points is not liftable, but its cube is, and lifts to the identity. An integral residue criterion supplies the CY test. A factorization localized on a contact connected sum is automatically CY. Unlike in the planar case, a CY factorization need not be the shortest. Once the fusion channels of the g pairs are fixed, Ising fusion determines the channel of the remaining pair, and braiding acts there only by scalars. Fibonacci fusion can leave that channel undetermined, and the powers of the cube then act by ten distinct relative phases on a single joint eigenspace, while the CY Stein filling stays fixed

papers.title_en: Search for new physics with charm data at BESIII
papers.abstract_en: Up to now, the Standard Model (SM) remains confronted with several outstanding issues, including the matter-antimatter asymmetry in the universe, as well as the masses, oscillations, and hierarchical structure of neutrinos. These challenges are closely tied to the naturalness and stability of the SM, and have motivated numerous proposals for new physics beyond the SM. The BESIII experiment has accumulated the world's largest data samples at the $J/ψ$ and $ψ(3686)$ resonances, providing an ideal environment for probing signatures of physics beyond the SM. This proceeding presents a summary of recent results published by the BESIII Collaboration on the searches for lepton/baryon number violation (LNV/BNV), charged lepton flavor violation (CLFV), and charmonium weak decays.

papers.title_en: Quantum State Search with Classical Interactive Advice
papers.abstract_en: We study whether a quantum verifier can find a hidden quantum state by exchanging classical messages with an unbounded prover who knows the state. The verifier has access to a reflection oracle about the target. For a Haar-random $n$-qubit target, we prove that achieving constant average fidelity with the target requires $(q+1)^2(B+1)=Ω(2^n)$, where $q$ is the number of verifier queries and $B$ is the total prover-to-verifier communication. The bound allows arbitrary classical interaction and unrestricted computation between queries. Our proof extends the lower bound of Aaronson and Kuperberg from a single classical proof to an arbitrary classical interaction. As a result, we obtain a quantum-oracle separation of UniqueQMA from QCIP with polynomially many classical messages. In particular, we give a unitary oracle $\mathcal{U}$ such that there exists a language $L\in\mathrm{UniqueQMA}^{\mathcal{U}}$ but $L\notin\mathrm{QCIP}^{\mathcal{U}}$. We further give an oracle construction for a notion known as QMA-QCIP[2] gap problem. This gives average case hardness for a QMA language under classical access to a QCIP[2] decision oracle and is used in establishing negative results on witness encryption and quantum indistinguishability obfuscation.

papers.title_en: Conjugate measurement-induced evolution towards maximally mixed states in quadratic quantum systems
papers.abstract_en: In an earlier work, we showed that, in the interaction-dominant setting, coupling the conjugate variables of a subsystem to distinct environment modes drives the subsystem to a maximally mixed state. Here, we extend the study to the full quadratic dynamics of a single-mode subsystem coupled to a two-mode environment, and identify the phase-space mechanism responsible for the asymptotic behavior. By tracking the exact reduced Weyl characteristic and Wigner functions, we demonstrate that they lose their dependence on local phase-space coordinates on every fixed compact region. In free-particle model, this happens for all values of coupling, whereas in the harmonic oscillator model, it happens above a critical value of the coupling. Under a finite-volume and momentum regularization, this behavior corresponds to the reduced subsystem approaching a maximally mixed state.

papers.title_en: Distributed Phase Tags: A Locality-Preserving Realification Compiler for Misty-State Quantum Programs
papers.abstract_en:
Complex amplitudes can be simulated over real Hilbert spaces by adjoining a two-dimensional real/imaginary degree of freedom. In a multipartite program, however, one globally shared phase tag is not a locality-preserving program transformation: every party would have to act on the same auxiliary system. We recast the distributed real simulation of multipartite quantum mechanics as a syntax-directed compiler into a real misty-state intermediate language. For $n$ parties we give explicit phase-reference codewords $|0\rangle_{P_n}$ and $|1\rangle_{P_n}$ on $n$ local tags and prove that the same real operator $J=XZ$ on any single tag realizes the logical action of multiplication by $i$. If a complex party-local gate is $A=A_R+iA_I$, its real translation is 
\[ \widehat A_j=A_R\otimes I+A_I\otimes J_j, \]
 which acts only on party $j$'s data and local phase tag. We prove an intertwining theorem for arbitrary finite party-local pure-state circuits, exact preservation of computational-basis measurement probabilities, preservation of the run-time interaction graph, and one-rebit-per-party overhead. For the canonical three-party GHZ program, the translation lies entirely inside the ordinary black-and-white misty gate fragment: controlled-$J$ replaces the complex phase operation, while the invariant $J_jJ_k|0\rangle_P=-|0\rangle_P$ transfers the required branch sign. This yields a short correctness proof for all four promised GHZ inputs and explains the earlier 64-path cancellation calculation at a single logical phase-code boundary. We distinguish this program realification problem from the weaker task of finding any real strategy with the same correlations, and state precisely which parts are known real-Hilbert-space simulation and which parts belong to the misty-language compilation layer developed here.

papers.title_en: Deformability of neutron-deficient Sn nuclei studied with semi-realistic interaction
papers.abstract_en: Although Sn nuclei have long been considered typical spherical nuclei, the $E2$ transitions in neutron-deficient Sn nuclei have posed a puzzle. We argue that their deformability may resolve this issue, based on self-consistent calculations with a semi-realistic interaction. The significant role of the pseudo-spin symmetry, which is attributed to the effects of the tensor force, is also discussed.

papers.title_en: Efficient Block Encodings for Ensembles of Molecular Hamiltonians
papers.abstract_en: Accurately characterizing molecular properties and reactivity often requires electronic-structure calculations across an ensemble of molecular geometries. Quantum algorithms that process such ensembles coherently could address this challenge, but they require Hamiltonian block encoding circuits that combine advanced factorization techniques with sublinear scaling in ensemble size. Here, we introduce SVD-THC, which extends tensor hypercontraction to sets of Hamiltonians defined at different nuclear geometries through a singular value decomposition of the ensemble. We use SVD-THC to construct a single multiplexed block encoding circuit for all geometries in an ensemble. We then evaluate the approach on ensembles generated by varying internal rotational coordinates in 1-bromo-2-chloroethane as well as in glycine and alanine dipeptides, corresponding to established model systems for peptide conformational landscapes, with up to 5,184 geometries. Across several resolutions of the internal-coordinate grids, the Toffoli complexity of the resulting circuits grows only weakly with the number of geometries, changing by at most 12% over grids that differ in size by up to 576$\times$. In an energy-thresholding circuit, this yields 35--200$\times$ fewer Toffoli gates than slicing together single-geometry block encodings. This approach could help make coherent processing of molecular geometry ensembles a useful primitive for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

papers.title_en: Thermodynamics of two-flavor isospin-asymmetric superfluid quark matter at next-to-leading order
papers.abstract_en: We study quark matter at high isospin asymmetry in the limit of vanishing baryon density, a state of matter governed by the condensation of charged pions. In the weak-coupling limit, this state of matter can be reliably described by conventional perturbative methods where a trivial ground state is assumed. However, since the condensate of charged pions generates a gap in the excitation spectrum of the quarks with a non-perturbative dependence on the strong coupling, corrections to the results from conventional perturbative methods arise. This situation is very reminiscent of the one encountered in isospin-symmetric quark matter at high baryon densities which is expected to be a color superconductor. In the present work, we calculate the thermodynamic properties of superfluid quark matter at high isospin asymmetry, zero temperature, and zero baryon density at next-to-leading order (NLO) in the coupling in the presence of a finite gap. We work in the limit of two massless quark flavors and further assume that the gap is small compared to the isospin chemical potential. Similar to the situation in color-superconducting quark matter at high baryon densities, we find that the gap-induced corrections lead to an increase of the pressure and the speed of sound above their values obtained for non-superfluid quark matter. Notably, starting from asymptotically high isospin asymmetries, these corrections lead to a systematic change of the slope of the speed of sound when the isospin asymmetry is decreased. We compare our results with recent lattice QCD and Dyson-Schwinger equation studies and find good agreement in the regimes where these methods are applicable.

papers.title_en: Coherent and Dissociative Photon-Induced Production in Herwig 7
papers.abstract_en:
We present a particle-level study of photon-induced production in Herwig~7, focusing on coherent, single-dissociative, and double-dissociative proton configurations. The simulation combines the Budnev elastic photon flux with an inelastic photon PDF, using the internal Herwig~7 matrix elements for $\gamma\gamma \to \ell^+\ell^-$ and $\gamma\gamma \to W^+W^- \to \ell^+\ell^-\nu\bar{\nu}$ as the central setup. Using a dedicated Rivet analysis, we compare hard-system kinematics, charged-particle activity, rapidity-gap observables, and distributions sensitive to forward proton remnants.

We find that variations in shower settings generally have modest effects on hard-system distributions in well-populated phase-space regions, whereas coherent and dissociative samples exhibit more pronounced differences in additional charged-particle activity and rapidity-gap observables. These results provide a useful baseline for modelling semi-exclusive photon-induced measurements at the LHC and identify observables that are particularly sensitive to dissociative activity in future Monte Carlo generator comparisons.

papers.title_en: Parton Fragmentation Functions
papers.abstract_en: This chapter provides a pedagogical and comprehensive introduction to parton fragmentation functions (FFs), the essential non-perturbative quantities in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) that describe the universal process of hadronization, the transition of quarks and gluons into observable hadrons. Formally defined as gauge-invariant matrix elements, the determination of FFs is achieved through global QCD analyses that synthesize world data from three primary processes: electron-positron annihilation, semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering, and proton-proton collisions. This chapter covers the theoretical foundations of FFs, including their operator definitions and properties, the experimental probes used to constrain them, and the methodologies of modern global analyses. The discussion is extended to more advanced topics, including dihadron FFs, the three-dimensional picture of hadronization provided by spin- and transverse-momentum-dependent FFs, and the modification of fragmentation in a nuclear medium, which is key to probe their fundamental properties.

papers.title_en: Measuring the Quantum Phase of Multiphoton Systems
papers.abstract_en: The quantum phase of a multiparticle system has remained a long-standing mystery in quantum physics. The absence of a phase operator that faithfully represents this physical quantity has prevented the formulation of a meaningful uncertainty relation with particle number. Here, we resolve this problem by measuring, for the first time, the quantum phase of multiparticle systems containing up to fifteen particles. We achieve this through a new quantum state tomography scheme that combines homodyne interferometry with photon-number-resolving detection. This approach enables us to reconstruct complementary photon-number and phase representations and establish the corresponding number-phase uncertainty relation. Our measurements further provide access to the mutually unbiased basis of a multiparticle system, a fundamental resource for multiparticle quantum information processing.
